content: Bisoprolol is a medication prescribed to treat high blood pressure, either on its own or in combination with other medications. It belongs to a class of drugs known as beta blockers. This medication works by slowing the heart rate and relaxing blood vessels, which reduces the workload on the heart. Bisoprolol is available in tablet form and is taken orally, usually once a day. To ensure consistent use, it is recommended to take it at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take bisoprolol exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. Your doctor will likely start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. While bisoprolol helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure it. It may take several weeks to experience the full benefits of the medication. Continue taking bisoprolol even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. If discontinuation is necessary, your doctor will likely reduce your dose gradually. In addition to treating high blood pressure, bisoprolol is sometimes used to manage heart failure. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Bisoprolol may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking bisoprolol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to bisoprolol or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention calcium channel blockers (e.g., diltiazem, verapamil), clonidine, guanethidine, medications for irregular heartbeat (e.g., disopyramide), other beta blockers, reserpine, and rifampin. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had asthma, other lung diseases, a slow heart rate, heart failure, heart, liver, or kidney disease, diabetes, severe allergies, circulation problems, or an overactive thyroid gland (hyperthyroidism). If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking bisoprolol, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking bisoprolol. Be aware that bisoprolol may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by bisoprolol, so use caution. If you have allergic reactions to various substances, note that your reactions may worsen while taking bisoprolol, and they may not respond to usual doses of injectable epinephrine. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of bisoprolol, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Bisoprolol may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience excessive tiredness, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle aches, or a runny nose. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience shortness of breath, swelling of the hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, unusual weight gain, or fainting. If you notice any unusual problems while taking this medication, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store bisoprolol in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include swelling of the hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; unusual weight gain; difficulty breathing or swallowing; dizziness; fainting; shakiness; sweating; confusion; blurred vision; headache; numbness or tingling of the mouth; weakness; extreme tiredness; sudden hunger; or pale skin. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Your blood pressure should be monitored regularly to assess your response to bisoprolol. Your doctor may ask you to check your pulse (heart rate). Ask your doctor or pharmacist to teach you how to take your pulse. If your pulse is faster or slower than it should be, contact your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
